data.task:
Fix the Flutter app CRAP ratchet offender in flutter_app for PR #1888.

## Target
`_handleComposerKey` in flutter_app/lib/ui/network/channel_composer.dart (line ~140, complexity 16, coverage 0.5909, CRAP 33.53 > 12.0 threshold).

## Change
Decompose the function following the codebase's existing patterns: extract cohesive private helpers (e.g. mention-autocomplete navigation, send vs newline decision, paste handling) so each method is small (CC ≤ 8 ideally) and the existing tests still cover the paths. TDD: check/extend the composer tests in flutter_app/test/network/ first so the extracted helpers are exercised (arrow keys, Enter send, Shift+Enter, paste).

## Also (low priority, only if trivial and safe)
- `NetworkSession._onWsEvent` in flutter_app/lib/network/network_session.dart:427 (CC 14): has almost no margin (measured 16.07 under network-only coverage; CI had it ≤12). If a simple decomposition is obvious, do it; otherwise leave it and note it.
- Same for channel_rail.dart `_deleteChannel` (CC 12) and `_RosterMemberTile.build` (CC 12) — only if trivial.

## Acceptance
1. `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json` (after `flutter test test/network/ --coverage`) reports `_handleComposerKey` CRAP ≤ 12.0, and no changed-file function above 12.0.
2. `flutter test test/network/` passes fully.
3. `flutter analyze` clean for changed files.
4. `dart format` applied to changed files.
Report filesChanged, CRAP before/after, and test results as JSON. Do not commit or push; do not touch files outside flutter_app/.
data.context:
# Goal
PR #1888 rework on branch `feat/1825-network-dap-scoped-joins` in /home/runner/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness (Flutter agent harness repo). CI "Flutter app CRAP ratchet" gate fails: `CRAP threshold exceeded: 33.53 > 12.0`. CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC per function; every function must measure ≤ 12.0 under the flutter-test-coverage pipeline.

# Verified facts (do not re-derive)
- The offender is `_handleComposerKey` in `flutter_app/lib/ui/network/channel_composer.dart` at line 140: complexity 16, line coverage 0.5909 → CRAP 33.53. It is the ONLY app offender over threshold in CI.
- Runner-up in a local network-suite-only coverage run (CI full-suite coverage may differ slightly): `NetworkSession._onWsEvent` in `flutter_app/lib/network/network_session.dart:427` (CC 14, cov 0.78 → 16.07) and `channel_rail.dart` `_deleteChannel` (CC 12 @ 0.935 → 12.039) / `_RosterMemberTile.build` (CC 12 @ 0.977 → 12.002). In CI these measured ≤ 12.0, but they have almost no margin — reducing their complexity a little is welcome IF trivial, do not break their tests.
- Local reproduction pipeline (approximates CI; takes ~2-4 min):
  1. `cd flutter_app && flutter test test/network/ --coverage` (need an empty `flutter_app/.env` file to exist: `touch flutter_app/.env`)
  2. `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json` and inspect `methods[].crap` for the changed files.
- After your decomposition, target: `_handleComposerKey` CRAP ≤ 12 with margin (aim CC ≤ 8 with the existing tests' coverage, or keep CC moderate and ensure the changed branches stay covered by existing network tests). Do NOT weaken the composer behavior: Enter sends, Shift+Enter/newline handling, paste-join interception, arrow-key mention navigation etc. must keep working — read the function and its tests first (`flutter_app/test/network/` has the composer tests; find them with grep).
- TDD: first add/extend a test in the project's standard test tree (`flutter_app/test/network/…`) that exercises the branches you extract (e.g. arrow-key navigation, enter-to-send, shift-enter insert), run it RED if feasible, then refactor GREEN.
- Do NOT touch anything outside `flutter_app/` except reading. Do NOT modify `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml` threshold (ratchet only-down). Do NOT run the full app suite (3973 tests) — `flutter test test/network/` is the verification scope; run `flutter analyze` on the files you changed too.
- Follow existing code style (trailing commas, doc comments on public members).
# Contract
The branch may receive commits from another agent concurrently in bin/, lib/src/hub/, lib/src/messaging/ and test/hub/ — never `git commit` or `git push` yourself; leave your changes uncommitted in the working tree ONLY in flutter_app/ paths, and report exactly what you changed. Avoid `git checkout`/`git restore` of any kind (would clobber the other agent's uncommitted work).

## Target
`_handleComposerKey` in flutter_app/lib/ui/network/channel_composer.dart (line ~140, complexity 16, coverage 0.5909, CRAP 33.53 > 12.0 threshold).

## Also (low priority, only if trivial and safe)
- `NetworkSession._onWsEvent` in flutter_app/lib/network/network_session.dart:427 (CC 14): has almost no margin (measured 16.07 under network-only coverage; CI had it ≤12). If a simple decomposition is obvious, do it; otherwise leave it and note it.

1. `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json` (after `flutter test test/network/ --coverage`) reports `_handleComposerKey` CRAP ≤ 12.0, and no changed-file function above 12.0.

3. `flutter analyze` clean for changed files.

Fix the Flutter app CRAP ratchet offender in flutter_app for PR #1888.

## Target
`_handleComposerKey` in flutter_app/lib/ui/network/channel_composer.dart (line ~140, complexity 16, coverage 0.5909, CRAP 33.53 > 12.0 threshold).

## Change
Decompose the function following the codebase's existing patterns: extract cohesive private helpers (e.g. mention-autocomplete navigation, send vs newline decision, paste handling) so each method is small (CC ≤ 8 ideally) and the existing tests still cover the paths. TDD: check/extend the composer tests in flutter_app/test/network/ first so the extracted helpers are exercised (arrow keys, Enter send, Shift+Enter, paste).

## Also (low priority, only if trivial and safe)
- `NetworkSession._onWsEvent` in flutter_app/lib/network/network_session.dart:427 (CC 14): has almost no margin (measured 16.07 under network-only coverage; CI had it ≤12). If a simple decomposition is obvious, do it; otherwise leave it and note it.
- Same for channel_rail.dart `_deleteChannel` (CC 12) and `_RosterMemberTile.build` (CC 12) — only if trivial.

## Acceptance
1. `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json` (after `flutter test test/network/ --coverage`) reports `_handleComposerKey` CRAP ≤ 12.0, and no changed-file function above 12.0.
2. `flutter test test/network/` passes fully.
3. `flutter analyze` clean for changed files.
4. `dart format` applied to changed files.
Report filesChanged, CRAP before/after, and test results as JSON. Do not commit or push; do not touch files outside flutter_app/.

CI "Flutter app CRAP ratchet" gate fails: `CRAP threshold exceeded: 33.53 > 12.0`. CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC per function; every function must measure ≤ 12.0 under the flutter-test-coverage pipeline.

# Verified facts (do not re-derive)
- The offender is `_handleComposerKey` in `flutter_app/lib/ui/network/channel_composer.dart` at line 140: complexity 16, line coverage 0.5909 → CRAP 33.53. It is the ONLY app offender over threshold in CI.
- Runner-up in a local network-suite-only coverage run (CI full-suite coverage may differ slightly): `NetworkSession._onWsEvent` in `flutter_app/lib/network/network_session.dart:427` (CC 14, cov 0.78 → 16.07) and `channel_rail.dart` `_deleteChannel` (CC 12 @ 0.935 → 12.039) / `_RosterMemberTile.build` (CC 12 @ 0.977 → 12.002).   1. `cd flutter_app && flutter test test/network/ --coverage` (need an empty `flutter_app/.env` file to exist: `touch flutter_app/.env`)
  2. `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json` and inspect `methods[].crap` for the changed files.
- After your decomposition, target: `_handleComposerKey` CRAP ≤ 12 with margin (aim CC ≤ 8 with the existing tests' coverage, or keep CC moderate and ensure the changed branches stay covered by existing network tests). Do NOT weaken the composer behavior: Enter sends, Shift+Enter/newline handling, paste-join interception, arrow-key mention navigation etc. must keep working — read the function and its tests first (`flutter_app/test/network/` has the composer tests; find them with grep).

# Contract
The branch may receive commits from another agent concurrently in bin/, lib/src/hub/, lib/src/messaging/ and test/hub/ — never `git commit` or `git push` yourself; leave your changes uncommitted in the working tree ONLY in flutter_app/ paths, and report exactly what you changed. Avoid `git checkout`/`git restore` of any kind (would clobber the other agent's uncommitted work).

data.task:
Fix the Flutter app CRAP ratchet offender in flutter_app for PR #1888.

## Target
`_handleComposerKey` in flutter_app/lib/ui/network/channel_composer.dart (line ~140, complexity 16, coverage 0.5909, CRAP 33.53 > 12.0 threshold).

## Change
Decompose the function following the codebase's existing patterns: extract cohesive private helpers (e.g. mention-autocomplete navigation, send vs newline decision, paste handling) so each method is small (CC ≤ 8 ideally) and the existing tests still cover the paths. TDD: check/extend the composer tests in flutter_app/test/network/ first so the extracted helpers are exercised (arrow keys, Enter send, Shift+Enter, paste).

## Also (low priority, only if trivial and safe)
- `NetworkSession._onWsEvent` in flutter_app/lib/network/network_session.dart:427 (CC 14): has almost no margin (measured 16.07 under network-only coverage; CI had it ≤12). If a simple decomposition is obvious, do it; otherwise leave it and note it.
- Same for channel_rail.dart `_deleteChannel` (CC 12) and `_RosterMemberTile.build` (CC 12) — only if trivial.

## Acceptance
1. `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json` (after `flutter test test/network/ --coverage`) reports `_handleComposerKey` CRAP ≤ 12.0, and no changed-file function above 12.0.
2. `flutter test test/network/` passes fully.
3. `flutter analyze` clean for changed files.
4. `dart format` applied to changed files.
Report filesChanged, CRAP before/after, and test results as JSON. Do not commit or push; do not touch files outside flutter_app/.

# Goal
PR #1888 rework on branch `feat/1825-network-dap-scoped-joins` in /home/runner/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness (Flutter agent harness repo). CI "Flutter app CRAP ratchet" gate fails: `CRAP threshold exceeded: 33.53 > 12.0`. CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC per function; every function must measure ≤ 12.0 under the flutter-test-coverage pipeline.

# Verified facts (do not re-derive)
- The offender is `_handleComposerKey` in `flutter_app/lib/ui/network/channel_composer.dart` at line 140: complexity 16, line coverage 0.5909 → CRAP 33.53. It is the ONLY app offender over threshold in CI.
- Runner-up in a local network-suite-only coverage run (CI full-suite coverage may differ slightly): `NetworkSession._onWsEvent` in `flutter_app/lib/network/network_session.dart:427` (CC 14, cov 0.78 → 16.07) and `channel_rail.dart` `_deleteChannel` (CC 12 @ 0.935 → 12.039) / `_RosterMemberTile.build` (CC 12 @ 0.977 → 12.002). In CI these measured ≤ 12.0, but they have almost no margin — reducing their complexity a little is welcome IF trivial, do not break their tests.
- Local reproduction pipeline (approximates CI; takes ~2-4 min):
  1. `cd flutter_app && flutter test test/network/ --coverage` (need an empty `flutter_app/.env` file to exist: `touch flutter_app/.env`)
  2. `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json` and inspect `methods[].crap` for the changed files.
- After your decomposition, target: `_handleComposerKey` CRAP ≤ 12 with margin (aim CC ≤ 8 with the existing tests' coverage, or keep CC moderate and ensure the changed branches stay covered by existing network tests). Do NOT weaken the composer behavior: Enter sends, Shift+Enter/newline handling, paste-join interception, arrow-key mention navigation etc. must keep working — read the function and its tests first (`flutter_app/test/network/` has the composer tests; find them with grep).
- TDD: first add/extend a test in the project's standard test tree (`flutter_app/test/network/…`) that exercises the branches you extract (e.g. arrow-key navigation, enter-to-send, shift-enter insert), run it RED if feasible, then refactor GREEN.
- Do NOT touch anything outside `flutter_app/` except reading. Do NOT modify `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml` threshold (ratchet only-down). Do NOT run the full app suite (3973 tests) — `flutter test test/network/` is the verification scope; run `flutter analyze` on the files you changed too.
- Follow existing code style (trailing commas, doc comments on public members).
# Contract
The branch may receive commits from another agent concurrently in bin/, lib/src/hub/, lib/src/messaging/ and test/hub/ — never `git commit` or `git push` yourself; leave your changes uncommitted in the working tree ONLY in flutter_app/ paths, and report exactly what you changed. Avoid `git checkout`/`git restore` of any kind (would clobber the other agent's uncommitted work).

data.name: appcrap
data.task:
Fix the Flutter app CRAP ratchet offender in flutter_app for PR #1888.

## Target
`_handleComposerKey` in flutter_app/lib/ui/network/channel_composer.dart (line ~140, complexity 16, coverage 0.5909, CRAP 33.53 > 12.0 threshold).

## Change
Decompose the function following the codebase's existing patterns: extract cohesive private helpers (e.g. mention-autocomplete navigation, send vs newline decision, paste handling) so each method is small (CC ≤ 8 ideally) and the existing tests still cover the paths. TDD: check/extend the composer tests in flutter_app/test/network/ first so the extracted helpers are exercised (arrow keys, Enter send, Shift+Enter, paste).

## Also (low priority, only if trivial and safe)
- `NetworkSession._onWsEvent` in flutter_app/lib/network/network_session.dart:427 (CC 14): has almost no margin (measured 16.07 under network-only coverage; CI had it ≤12). If a simple decomposition is obvious, do it; otherwise leave it and note it.
- Same for channel_rail.dart `_deleteChannel` (CC 12) and `_RosterMemberTile.build` (CC 12) — only if trivial.

## Acceptance
1. `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json` (after `flutter test test/network/ --coverage`) reports `_handleComposerKey` CRAP ≤ 12.0, and no changed-file function above 12.0.
2. `flutter test test/network/` passes fully.
3. `flutter analyze` clean for changed files.
4. `dart format` applied to changed files.
Report filesChanged, CRAP before/after, and test results as JSON. Do not commit or push; do not touch files outside flutter_app/.
data.context:
# Goal
PR #1888 rework on branch `feat/1825-network-dap-scoped-joins` in /home/runner/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness (Flutter agent harness repo). CI "Flutter app CRAP ratchet" gate fails: `CRAP threshold exceeded: 33.53 > 12.0`. CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC per function; every function must measure ≤ 12.0 under the flutter-test-coverage pipeline.

# Verified facts (do not re-derive)
- The offender is `_handleComposerKey` in `flutter_app/lib/ui/network/channel_composer.dart` at line 140: complexity 16, line coverage 0.5909 → CRAP 33.53. It is the ONLY app offender over threshold in CI.
- Runner-up in a local network-suite-only coverage run (CI full-suite coverage may differ slightly): `NetworkSession._onWsEvent` in `flutter_app/lib/network/network_session.dart:427` (CC 14, cov 0.78 → 16.07) and `channel_rail.dart` `_deleteChannel` (CC 12 @ 0.935 → 12.039) / `_RosterMemberTile.build` (CC 12 @ 0.977 → 12.002). In CI these measured ≤ 12.0, but they have almost no margin — reducing their complexity a little is welcome IF trivial, do not break their tests.
- Local reproduction pipeline (approximates CI; takes ~2-4 min):
  1. `cd flutter_app && flutter test test/network/ --coverage` (need an empty `flutter_app/.env` file to exist: `touch flutter_app/.env`)
  2. `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json` and inspect `methods[].crap` for the changed files.
- After your decomposition, target: `_handleComposerKey` CRAP ≤ 12 with margin (aim CC ≤ 8 with the existing tests' coverage, or keep CC moderate and ensure the changed branches stay covered by existing network tests). Do NOT weaken the composer behavior: Enter sends, Shift+Enter/newline handling, paste-join interception, arrow-key mention navigation etc. must keep working — read the function and its tests first (`flutter_app/test/network/` has the composer tests; find them with grep).
- TDD: first add/extend a test in the project's standard test tree (`flutter_app/test/network/…`) that exercises the branches you extract (e.g. arrow-key navigation, enter-to-send, shift-enter insert), run it RED if feasible, then refactor GREEN.
- Do NOT touch anything outside `flutter_app/` except reading. Do NOT modify `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml` threshold (ratchet only-down). Do NOT run the full app suite (3973 tests) — `flutter test test/network/` is the verification scope; run `flutter analyze` on the files you changed too.
- Follow existing code style (trailing commas, doc comments on public members).
# Contract
The branch may receive commits from another agent concurrently in bin/, lib/src/hub/, lib/src/messaging/ and test/hub/ — never `git commit` or `git push` yourself; leave your changes uncommitted in the working tree ONLY in flutter_app/ paths, and report exactly what you changed. Avoid `git checkout`/`git restore` of any kind (would clobber the other agent's uncommitted work).

data.task:
Fix the Flutter app CRAP ratchet offender in flutter_app for PR #1888.

## Target
`_handleComposerKey` in flutter_app/lib/ui/network/channel_composer.dart (line ~140, complexity 16, coverage 0.5909, CRAP 33.53 > 12.0 threshold).

## Change
Decompose the function following the codebase's existing patterns: extract cohesive private helpers (e.g. mention-autocomplete navigation, send vs newline decision, paste handling) so each method is small (CC ≤ 8 ideally) and the existing tests still cover the paths. TDD: check/extend the composer tests in flutter_app/test/network/ first so the extracted helpers are exercised (arrow keys, Enter send, Shift+Enter, paste).

## Also (low priority, only if trivial and safe)
- `NetworkSession._onWsEvent` in flutter_app/lib/network/network_session.dart:427 (CC 14): has almost no margin (measured 16.07 under network-only coverage; CI had it ≤12). If a simple decomposition is obvious, do it; otherwise leave it and note it.
- Same for channel_rail.dart `_deleteChannel` (CC 12) and `_RosterMemberTile.build` (CC 12) — only if trivial.

## Acceptance
1. `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json` (after `flutter test test/network/ --coverage`) reports `_handleComposerKey` CRAP ≤ 12.0, and no changed-file function above 12.0.
2. `flutter test test/network/` passes fully.
3. `flutter analyze` clean for changed files.
4. `dart format` applied to changed files.
Report filesChanged, CRAP before/after, and test results as JSON. Do not commit or push; do not touch files outside flutter_app/.

# Goal
PR #1888 rework on branch `feat/1825-network-dap-scoped-joins` in /home/runner/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness (Flutter agent harness repo). CI "Flutter app CRAP ratchet" gate fails: `CRAP threshold exceeded: 33.53 > 12.0`. CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC per function; every function must measure ≤ 12.0 under the flutter-test-coverage pipeline.

# Verified facts (do not re-derive)
- The offender is `_handleComposerKey` in `flutter_app/lib/ui/network/channel_composer.dart` at line 140: complexity 16, line coverage 0.5909 → CRAP 33.53. It is the ONLY app offender over threshold in CI.
- Runner-up in a local network-suite-only coverage run (CI full-suite coverage may differ slightly): `NetworkSession._onWsEvent` in `flutter_app/lib/network/network_session.dart:427` (CC 14, cov 0.78 → 16.07) and `channel_rail.dart` `_deleteChannel` (CC 12 @ 0.935 → 12.039) / `_RosterMemberTile.build` (CC 12 @ 0.977 → 12.002). In CI these measured ≤ 12.0, but they have almost no margin — reducing their complexity a little is welcome IF trivial, do not break their tests.
- Local reproduction pipeline (approximates CI; takes ~2-4 min):
  1. `cd flutter_app && flutter test test/network/ --coverage` (need an empty `flutter_app/.env` file to exist: `touch flutter_app/.env`)
  2. `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json` and inspect `methods[].crap` for the changed files.
- After your decomposition, target: `_handleComposerKey` CRAP ≤ 12 with margin (aim CC ≤ 8 with the existing tests' coverage, or keep CC moderate and ensure the changed branches stay covered by existing network tests). Do NOT weaken the composer behavior: Enter sends, Shift+Enter/newline handling, paste-join interception, arrow-key mention navigation etc. must keep working — read the function and its tests first (`flutter_app/test/network/` has the composer tests; find them with grep).
- TDD: first add/extend a test in the project's standard test tree (`flutter_app/test/network/…`) that exercises the branches you extract (e.g. arrow-key navigation, enter-to-send, shift-enter insert), run it RED if feasible, then refactor GREEN.
- Do NOT touch anything outside `flutter_app/` except reading. Do NOT modify `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml` threshold (ratchet only-down). Do NOT run the full app suite (3973 tests) — `flutter test test/network/` is the verification scope; run `flutter analyze` on the files you changed too.
- Follow existing code style (trailing commas, doc comments on public members).

The branch may receive commits from another agent concurrently in bin/, lib/src/hub/, lib/src/messaging/ and test/hub/ — never `git commit` or `git push` yourself; leave your changes uncommitted in the working tree ONLY in flutter_app/ paths, and report exactly what you changed. Avoid `git checkout`/`git restore` of any kind (would clobber the other agent's uncommitted work).

Fix the Flutter app CRAP ratchet offender in flutter_app for PR #1888.

## Target
`_handleComposerKey` in flutter_app/lib/ui/network/channel_composer.dart (line ~140, complexity 16, coverage 0.5909, CRAP 33.53 > 12.0 threshold).

## Change
Decompose the function following the codebase's existing patterns: extract cohesive private helpers (e.g. mention-autocomplete navigation, send vs newline decision, paste handling) so each method is small (CC ≤ 8 ideally) and the existing tests still cover the paths. TDD: check/extend the composer tests in flutter_app/test/network/ first so the extracted helpers are exercised (arrow keys, Enter send, Shift+Enter, paste).

## Also (low priority, only if trivial and safe)
- `NetworkSession._onWsEvent` in flutter_app/lib/network/network_session.dart:427 (CC 14): has almost no margin (measured 16.07 under network-only coverage; CI had it ≤12). If a simple decomposition is obvious, do it; otherwise leave it and note it.
- Same for channel_rail.dart `_deleteChannel` (CC 12) and `_RosterMemberTile.build` (CC 12) — only if trivial.

1. `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json` (after `flutter test test/network/ --coverage`) reports `_handleComposerKey` CRAP ≤ 12.0, and no changed-file function above 12.0.

3. `flutter analyze` clean for changed files.
4. `dart format` applied to changed files.
Report filesChanged, CRAP before/after, and test results as JSON. Do not commit or push; do not touch files outside flutter_app/.

data.task:
Fix the Flutter app CRAP ratchet offender in flutter_app for PR #1888.

## Target
`_handleComposerKey` in flutter_app/lib/ui/network/channel_composer.dart (line ~140, complexity 16, coverage 0.5909, CRAP 33.53 > 12.0 threshold).

## Change
Decompose the function following the codebase's existing patterns: extract cohesive private helpers (e.g. mention-autocomplete navigation, send vs newline decision, paste handling) so each method is small (CC ≤ 8 ideally) and the existing tests still cover the paths. TDD: check/extend the composer tests in flutter_app/test/network/ first so the extracted helpers are exercised (arrow keys, Enter send, Shift+Enter, paste).

## Also (low priority, only if trivial and safe)
- `NetworkSession._onWsEvent` in flutter_app/lib/network/network_session.dart:427 (CC 14): has almost no margin (measured 16.07 under network-only coverage; CI had it ≤12). If a simple decomposition is obvious, do it; otherwise leave it and note it.
- Same for channel_rail.dart `_deleteChannel` (CC 12) and `_RosterMemberTile.build` (CC 12) — only if trivial.

## Acceptance
1. `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json` (after `flutter test test/network/ --coverage`) reports `_handleComposerKey` CRAP ≤ 12.0, and no changed-file function above 12.0.
2. `flutter test test/network/` passes fully.
3. `flutter analyze` clean for changed files.
4. `dart format` applied to changed files.
Report filesChanged, CRAP before/after, and test results as JSON. Do not commit or push; do not touch files outside flutter_app/.

- The offender is `_handleComposerKey` in `flutter_app/lib/ui/network/channel_composer.dart` at line 140: complexity 16, line coverage 0.5909 → CRAP 33.53. It is the ONLY app offender over threshold in CI.

- After your decomposition, target: `_handleComposerKey` CRAP ≤ 12 with margin (aim CC ≤ 8 with the existing tests' coverage, or keep CC moderate and ensure the changed branches stay covered by existing network tests). Do NOT weaken the composer behavior: Enter sends, Shift+Enter/newline handling, paste-join interception, arrow-key mention navigation etc. must keep working — read the function and its tests first (`flutter_app/test/network/` has the composer tests; find them with grep).

- Follow existing code style (trailing commas, doc comments on public members).

The branch may receive commits from another agent concurrently in bin/, lib/src/hub/, lib/src/messaging/ and test/hub/ — never `git commit` or `git push` yourself; leave your changes uncommitted in the working tree ONLY in flutter_app/ paths, and report exactly what you changed. guards:
    name: CRAP + duplication
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes, test-core]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.docs != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared/app/docs changes — guards green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.docs == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.docs == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      # Same scope gate as every other step here: on a skipped (app-only)
      # PR no dart SDK is set up, so an unconditional pub get dies with 127.
      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:

`test/hub/hub_messaging_frames_test.dart`:
- A `_FrameHub` raw HttpServer+WebSocket that: on 'hello' → welcome (agentId derived); on 'join' for channel 'ok-channel' → `{op:'joined',channel:'ok-channel'}`; for 'denied-channel' → `{op:'error',code:'access_denied',msg:'nope'}`; on 'send' with channel → broadcast a channel_msg frame to ALL sockets (echo) so the receiving repo gets a public channel message: `{op:'channel_msg', id:'m1', channel:'ok-channel', from:<other-agent-id>, ts:..., ciphertext: base64(json {'text':'hello room'})}`.
- Test 1: joined + channel mail: repo.joinChannel('ok-channel') completes (covers _onJoined, joinChannel happy path, waitForConnection covered already), then deliver a channel_msg from another agent → drain() includes AgentMessage toId '#ok-channel' with text 'hello room' (covers _onChannelMsg public path + _decodePublicChannelPayload JSON branch + _inbox add).
- Test 2: raw UTF-8 payload tolerated (covers the catch branch of _decodePublicChannelPayload): ciphertext = base64(utf8 'plain foreign text') → text passes through.
- Test 3: access_denied: joinChannel('denied-channel') throws StateError ('hub denied channel join') — covers _onErrorFrame access_denied branch incl joinOrder logic.
- Test 4: error without joinOrder (code other than access_denied or joinOrder empty): send error frame when no join pending → covers the log branch ('hub error: code msg') — observable via onLog.

Two client repos? For the channel echo I can have the FAKE hub itself inject the channel_msg frame (server-initiated) after the join — simpler: after answering join 'ok-channel', server sends channel_msg from a fabricated 'other-agent'. But _onChannelMsg drops when `from == agentId` or channel not in _channels — from must differ from receiver's agentId and repo must have joined 'ok-channel'. Also the frame needs... `id` non-empty, not in _seenFrameIds.

Our repo's register flow may send extra fields; keep the switch lenient (ignore unknown ops).

Timing: repo.start() → dial → hello → welcome completes. Then joinChannel('ok-channel') → sendJoin → fake replies joined → completer completes. Then fake pushes channel_msg (maybe on a small delay or immediately after joined). Drain: repo.inbox/drain()? What's the repo's drain API? In hub tests: `_inbox.add(AgentMessage...)`; the drain boundary — used by the plugin host. Check the repo's public API: `drain()` probably `Future<List<AgentMessage>> drain()`. Grep quickly. # PR #1888 Rework — Scoped DAP channel joins (gh-1825)

Head after rework: `06aa778fba` (pushed; includes the `origin/main` merge and
both rework legs' commits).

## Issues/Notes

- **No open inline review threads** on the PR — the only discussion item is
  the bot-generated red-head arming notice, which the census explicitly
  excludes as a reply target (`threadId: null`, `bot: true`). Every real
  finding arrived as CI failures. `outputs/review_replies.json` is therefore
  `{ "replies": [] }`.
- Two rework legs ran concurrently on this branch (CRAP gate + PTY failures);
  their commits (`8e257a4682`, `0beeb8321e`, `3a129c31a9`) are merged in.
  One real merge bug was found and fixed while driving the menu flows in a
  unit harness: the default fallback stopper in `_dapStop` ignored the hub
  URL argument the injected `hubStopper` seam now receives.
- Local-only flake note: a few headless integration tests fail **in this
  sandbox only** with provider `429 rate limited` retries (they dial the real
  model endpoint) and one 100x40 PTY grid assertion is timing-sensitive. None
  of these appear in the CI red list for this PR; every CI-owned failure is
  addressed below and passes locally.

### Owned CI violations (all fixed)

| Check | Offender (path:line at red head) | Status / fix |
|---|---|---|
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `HubPluginHost._dapStart` CC 24 @ 0% | **fixed** — decomposed into `_ensureDapSessionSecret` / `_promptForHubPassword` / `_ensureLocalHub` / `_applyHubPassword` / `_persistLocalHubUrl` / `_startLocalConnection` / `_connectLocalHub`; each ≤ CC 3, exercised by the new unit tests |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `HubPluginHost._menuConnect` CC 15 @ 0% | **fixed** — decomposed into `_startHubForMenu` (bounded 8 s start) / `_menuConnectPrompted` / `_promptMenuConnection` / `_prepareMenuConnection` / `_connectMenuInput` |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `HubPluginHost._dapMenu` CC 9 @ 0% | **fixed** — the choice dispatch runs through `_dapMenu`'s action map, covered by menu unit tests (every choice is picked) |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `HubPluginHost._dapSlash` CC 9 @ 0% | **fixed** — split into `_dapDefault` (menu vs one-line status) / `_dapArgs` / `_dapConnectArgs` |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `HubPluginHost.publicChannelFor` CC 8 @ 0% | **fixed** — unit test: no effective memberships → `false` |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `HubPluginHost._hasPendingHubMail` CC 7 @ 0% | **fixed** — decomposed into a `_peekAnyPending`-style predicate; covered via the host registration path |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `HubPluginHost._dapTools` CC 8 @ 9.8% | **fixed** — each of the 5 tool closures is executed by unit tests (`dap_status`, `dap_peers`, `dap_dm`, `dap_invite`, `dap_connect`) |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `HubPluginHost._menuSetSecret` CC 6 @ 0% | **fixed** — decomposed into `_promptMasterSecret` / `_setSessionMasterSecret` / `_startAfterSettingSecret`; the post-secret start is now bounded to 8 s like `_startHubForMenu` so a dead hub can no longer wedge the menu |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `HubPluginHost._resolvePeer` CC 6 @ 0% | **fixed** — peer-not-found error path covered by the `dap_dm` unit test |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `HubPluginHost._connect` CC 10 @ 40% | **fixed** — decomposed into `_connectWithScopedBoot` / `_applyBootMembership` / `_applyScopedIdentity` / `_tryScopedBootConnect` / `_printBootConnectError`; env writes go through the read-only-safe `_setEnvironmentValue` |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `HubPluginHost._syncRuntimeMemberships` CC 18 @ 79.3% | **fixed** — decomposed into dial/throttle/env/join helpers (dial decision, 10 s throttle arm, scoped identity env, per-channel accept+join loop) |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `HubPluginHost._networkChannels` CC 9 @ 48.6% | **fixed** — row printing and the manage menu extracted; bare `/network` and usage-error paths covered by unit tests |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `HubPluginHost._printStatus` CC 4 @ 0% | **fixed** — split into disabled/hub printers; both covered |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `HubPluginHost._drainHubMail` CC 7 @ 52% | **fixed** — leave-filter extracted |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `HubPluginHost._networkSlash` CC 14 @ 80.8% | **fixed** — arg parsing/menu dispatch extracted; `join`/unknown-subcommand usage paths covered |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `MacOsDapChannelKeychain.read` CC 4 @ 0% | **fixed** — new unit test covers the unavailable-CLI path (graceful null on Linux CI) |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `DapScopedMemberships.join` CC 16 @ 100% | **fixed** — decomposed into scope-specific join steps + invite-secret encryption helper (behavior unchanged) |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `DapScopedMemberships._resolvePassphrase` CC 13 @ 88.2% | **fixed** — auto-provisioning extracted; existing passphrase tests pass unchanged |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `HubMessagingRepository._onFrame` CC 19 @ 93.8% | **fixed** — switch arms extracted into `_onWelcome` / `_onJoined` / `_onErrorFrame`; `_onFrame` now CC 10 (measures 10.02 under the local suite) |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `HubMessagingRepository._dialOnce` CC 14 @ 94.7% | **fixed** — decomposed into `_connectSocket` + dial/handshake helpers; `_dialOnce` now CC 11 (measures 11.00) |
| CRAP + duplication (`guards`) | `parseDapInviteFlexible` CC 14 @ 100% | **fixed** — the `fa dap import '…'` unwrap and bare-channel-id parsing extracted; all 17 existing parser tests keep passing |
| Flutter app CRAP ratchet | `_handleComposerKey` CC 16 @ 59.1% → CRAP 33.53 | **fixed** — decomposed into `_handleMentionMenuKey` (CC 7) / `_handleEnterKey` (CC 4); CRAP now 8.0 at coverage 1.00 via 3 new widget tests (Enter sends, Shift+Enter stays editable, Escape dismisses) |
| PTY/CLI shards (×3) | 5 `UnsupportedError` failures in `dap_unconfigured_test` / `dap_slash_flow_test` / `dap_start_test` (read-only const env map at plugin registration) | **fixed** (leg 2, merged) — registration-time env writes tolerate read-only embedder maps; all 5 pass locally (12/12 in `dap_start_test` + `dap_unconfigured_test`, plus `dap_slash_flow_test`, `dap_tui_menu_test`, `dap_chatter_loop_test`, `dap_identity_notice_test`) |

Foreign / infra reds: none — every red check names files this PR changes.

## Approach

TDD per finding: the exact scenario from each CI row was first reproduced or
confirmed uncovered, then the minimal decomposition/refactor landed and the
new/extended tests went green. Because the CRAP gate measures the merged
unit-suite lcov (which excludes `integration`-tagged tests), the
previously-0%-covered menu/slash/tool surface needed an untagged in-VM driver
(`hub_plugin_menu_flow_test.dart`, raw-socket frame tests); the app-side
composer work added failing-branch widget tests first, then the key-handler
split. No production behavior was intentionally changed: the extractions
move existing branches into named helpers, env writes go through a
read-only-safe setter, and the two bounded-start additions (`_startHubForMenu`
idempotently already existed; `_startAfterSettingSecret` now matches it at
8 s) only cap how long a dead hub can block a menu action.

## Files Modified

- `bin/fah_hub_plugin.dart` — CRAP decompositions across the table above;
  `_setEnvironmentValue` read-only-safe env setter; bounded post-secret start.
- `bin/fah_dap_scoped.dart` — `join` / `_resolvePassphrase` decomposition.
- `lib/src/messaging/hub_messaging_repository.dart` — `_onFrame` / `_dialOnce`
  decomposition (pure dispatch/move, no wire-behavior change).
- `lib/src/hub/dap_invite_import.dart` — `parseDapInviteFlexible`
  decomposition.
- `test/hub/hub_plugin_menu_flow_test.dart` — unit coverage of `/dap`
  args/menu flows, `dap_*` tools, `publicChannelFor`, `/network` validation
  (19 tests; deterministic settle-based boot).
- `test/hub/hub_messaging_frames_test.dart` — NEW: raw-socket hub driving
  `joined` / `error` frames and PUBLIC channel mail (covers the extracted
  `_onWelcome`/`_onJoined`/`_onErrorFrame` and the public decode path).
- `test/hub/dap_macos_keychain_test.dart` — NEW: keychain read degrades to
  null without the `security` CLI.
- `flutter_app/lib/ui/network/channel_composer.dart`,
  `flutter_app/lib/network/network_session.dart`,
  `flutter_app/lib/ui/network/channel_rail.dart` + their tests — app-side
  CRAP fixes (composer 33.53 → 8.0; `_onWsEvent` 16.07 → 9.21; rail helpers
  ≤ 10.05).

## Test Coverage

- `dart test test/hub/ test/cli/fah_dap_import_test.dart` — **328 passed**,
  0 failed (post-merge tree; includes the frames, menu-flow, repository,
  scoped, passphrase, fabric, and command suites).
- `dart test test/hub/hub_plugin_menu_flow_test.dart` — 19/19.
- `dart test test/hub/hub_messaging_frames_test.dart` — 2/2.
- `dart test test/cli/fah_dap_import_test.dart test/hub/dap_invite_flexible_test.dart` — 25/25.
- `dart test test/hub/dap_command_test.dart test/hub/hub_plugin_host_test.dart test/integration/dap_slash_flow_test.dart test/integration/dap_start_test.dart` — 43/43 (the CI PTY failures among them).
- `dart test test/integration/dap_start_test.dart test/integration/dap_unconfigured_test.dart` — 12/12.
- CRAP re-measurement on the final tree: `bin/fah_hub_plugin.dart`,
  `bin/fah_dap_scoped.dart`, `lib/src/hub/dap_invite_import.dart` — **all
  functions ≤ 12.0** (166 methods; worst exactly 12.0 at CC 3 / 0%);
  `hub_messaging_repository.dart` — `_onFrame` 10.02, `_dialOnce` 11.00,

- `cd flutter_app && flutter test test/network/` — 389/389; app crap4dart:
  every function in the changed files ≤ 12.0 (max pre-existing `_build`

### 1. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6wGf8Z` — **unknown** (`bin/fah_hub_plugin.dart:379`)

🚨 **BLOCKING: DAP env secrets are never registered with the redaction pipeline (ticket AC8/AC14)**

The ticket is explicit: *"CI test: the env values never appear in any session JSONL/tool result (**redactor registered for them**, the `SessionKeysStore` pattern)"* (`input/gh-1825/ticket.md`, Security & secrets). This PR adds the env contract (`DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` with **plaintext** `priv`s, `DAP_CLIENT_SECRET`, `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE`) but never registers those values anywhere. I grepped the whole diff: no `registerSecret` / `buildSecretRedactor` / redaction-pipeline touch.

Concretely: those variables live in the real process env (CI sets them there), so **every bash child inherits them**. A single `env` / `printenv DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` / `echo $DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE` tool call puts plaintext channel private keys and hub credentials into the tool result → the session JSONL and the model context, unmasked. The L9 entropy layer is not a substitute: base64 with standard-alphabet `/` splits into tokens below the entropy gate, and human-memorable passphrases / short hub secrets fail Shannon heuristics by construction. There is also no test covering this (the AC8 "CI test" does not exist in `test/`).

Fix: register `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON`, `DAP_CLIENT_SECRET`, `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE` (and the decrypted privs / auto-provisioned passphrases held in `_memoryOnlyKeys`/`_memoryOnlySecrets`) into `RedactionPipeline.registerSecret` at startup (same pattern as `buildSecretRedactor` in `lib/src/cli/startup.dart:1054`), plus a byte-scan test that these values never appear in a session JSONL or tool result.

### 2. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6wGf9t` — **unknown** (`lib/src/messaging/hub_messaging_repository.dart`)

🚨 **BLOCKING: the pure-Dart hub repository cannot open `fanet1` frames — the app DAP path drops private-channel mail the CLI fabric now sends**

The same PR makes the CLI fabric send private channel frames as `fanet1` (`bin/hub_fabric_repository.dart:147` → `client.sendChannelFanet1(...)`), and the CHANGELOG announces *"Inbound channel frames open `fanet1` first and fall back to legacy `dap/1` payloads"*. But that inbound open exists only in the vendored `fa_hub_client` 0.2.11 — **not here**. The Flutter app cannot import that package (its barrel pulls `dart:io`, per `flutter_app/lib/network/envelope_codec.dart:19` doc), so its DAP membership rides THIS repository (`flutter_app/lib/services/agent_network_controller.dart:226`), and `_onChannelMsg` (this file, line 532) only understands:

- keyless → `_decodePublicChannelPayload`, or
- keyed → `hubDecryptPayloadWithKeyPair` expecting the **raw dap1 layout** `base64(nonce(12) || ct || tag)` with the sender key from whois.

A `fanet1` payload is `base64(0x01 || spk(32) || nonce(12) || ct || tag(16))` (`flutter_app/lib/network/envelope_codec.dart:30-36`). Decoding it as dap1 takes `nonce = raw[0..12)` = `0x01 || spk[0..11]` → AEAD tag mismatch → the frame is dropped at line 572 (`dropped undecryptable channel mail`). Result: an app enrolled via the DAP path (`dap_enrollment_service`) never receives private-channel messages from CLI/fabric agents, in exactly the interop scenario this PR headlines. The app's fa_network path handles `fanet1` via `EnvelopeCodec`; this repository needs the equivalent open (detect `data[0] == 1 && data.length >= 61`, extract `spk`, skip the 33-byte header before the AEAD) plus a round-trip test against `EnvelopeCodec.encrypt`.

### 3. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6wGf-6` — **unknown** (`bin/fah_hub_plugin.dart`)

🚨 **BLOCKING: undecryptable private memberships are classified as PUBLIC — the fabric then sends plaintext into a private channel**

`_isPublicMembership` decides the wire format from the **runtime-decrypted** membership: `membership.pub == null || membership.priv == null` → "public". But `DapScopedMemberships.runtimeEffective()` (`bin/fah_dap_scoped.dart:465`) yields `priv: null` whenever the stored `dapkey1.` envelope could not be decrypted (missing passphrase — loud warning, "joined without keys, primary job proceeds"). For a PRIVATE channel that means: `pub != null`, `priv == null` → this check returns **true** → `HubFabricRepository.send` (`bin/hub_fabric_repository.dart:131`) takes the public-showcase branch and emits `base64({"text": …})` — **no encryption at all** — into a channel whose trust model is E2E ("the hub never sees plaintext", `_aboutText` in this file).

So one environment failure (no `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE`, no Keychain hit) silently downgrades every outbound channel message from that agent to hub-readable plaintext, and keyed members render "(unable to decrypt)". The public/private decision must come from the **stored** membership shape (a truly public channel has `pub == null` at rest; a stored envelope or plaintext `priv` means private), not from runtime decryption success — and when the key genuinely cannot be resolved, the send should refuse/queue with a loud error rather than downgrade.

### 4. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6wGgAB` — **unknown** (`lib/src/hub/dap_key_envelope.dart:120`)

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: unbounded PBKDF2 iteration count from the envelope — DoS via committed config or env**

`iterations` is read straight out of the (attacker-influenceable) envelope JSON with no sanity bound, then fed to `Pbkdf2(iterations: …)`. A `.fah/dap.json` committed to a repo someone clones (the ticket's v3 stance is that this file MAY be committed and team-shared), or a `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` env entry, can carry `"iter": 1000000000` — with `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE` set (CI always has it), boot pays ~hours of KDF per envelope before the AEAD tag check ever runs. The format stores the count as data specifically so tests can lower it; it needs an upper bound too (e.g. reject `iter > 5_000_000` with the existing `FormatException` path, which already surfaces one clear warning and proceeds with the primary job). Cheap fix, closes a real boot-DoS slot.

### 5. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6wGgAr` — **unknown** (`lib/src/hub/dap_env_channels.dart`)

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: wrong-typed `pub`/`priv` in `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` crashes the parse instead of warn-and-skip**

The module header promises "a malformed ENTRY produces a loud warning and is skipped — DAP is never a hard dependency of the agent's primary job", and the tests cover missing `channel` / non-object entries. But `pub: entry['pub'] as String?` / `priv: entry['priv'] as String?` throw an **uncaught `TypeError`** when the values aren't strings — e.g. `[{"channel":"team","priv":123}]` or a YAML-ism pasted into the CI secret (verified: `type 'int' is not a subtype of type 'String?'`). That escapes `parseDapEnvChannels` entirely and propagates into `DapScopedMemberships.union()` → `seedOverlay()` / `runtimeEffective()` / `acceptsChannel()`, i.e. every membership-touching path, contrary to the documented contract. Use tolerant reads (`entry['pub'] is String ? … : null` + a skip warning) or wrap the per-entry body in try/catch like `_loadSession` does.

### 6. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6wGgBm` — **unknown** (`bin/fah_dap_scoped.dart:485`)

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the runtime overlay persists PLAINTEXT channel keys and is never cleaned up**

`seedOverlay()` writes the **decrypted** union keys to `$HOME/.dap/runtime/channels-$pid.json` (060 best-effort). That contradicts the ticket's core secret rule — *"Plaintext `priv` exists only in memory — and in the pure-env CI path"* (`input/gh-1825/ticket.md`) — in two ways:

1. It is a third at-rest plaintext-key location nobody accounts for (the threat model covers global/project/session stores only).
2. Nothing ever deletes it: one file per pid accumulates in `~/.dap/runtime/` forever (grep: no delete/unlink anywhere in `bin/`). Every past run's channel keys stay on disk, and the pid naming guarantees unbounded growth.

Please delete the overlay on shutdown (plugin dispose / CLI `finally`) or use a single stable name rewritten atomically, and note the overlay explicitly in the secrets table if it must exist.

### 7. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6wGgCW` — **unknown** (`bin/fah_dap_scoped.dart:636`)

⚠️ **IMPORTANT (deviation to confirm against the ticket): global-scope join writes PLAINTEXT `priv` to `~/.dap/channels.json`**

The ticket's v3 secrets table says the global surface holds **encrypted** entries: *"global | `~/.dap/channels.json` (encrypted entries) | OS Keychain, else one prompt"* — while session/project/env get the `dapkey1` envelope. This path instead persists the invite's plaintext keypair through the legacy `persistChannelKeys`, so a `/network` global-scope private join leaves readable key material at rest (same as today's `fa dap import`, which is presumably why: REG-* demands byte-equivalence between the old import and the new global join).

If byte-equivalence with `fa dap import` is the reason, please say so explicitly in `docs/dap.md` and the join warning — right now the CLI advertises "private channel joined" while the on-disk posture differs from the ticket's table and from the session/project scopes the wizard just offered. If it is not the reason, route global joins through `encryptChannelPriv` like the other scopes.

### 8. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6wGgDc` — **unknown** (`bin/fah_dap_scoped.dart:291`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: `_loadProject` silently drops ALL project memberships on one malformed entry**

The whole read/parse sits in one `try/on Object → return const []`, so a single malformed record (e.g. an older record missing the required `scope` field, which makes `DapChannelMembership.fromJson` throw) discards the entire project store with no `loadWarnings` entry — while `_loadSession` right below adds one warning per bad record and keeps the rest. A half-corrupt `.fah/dap.json` after a bad merge would quietly unjoin every channel for every agent booted from the folder. Iterate per entry like `_loadSession` does.

## Automated Code Review — BLOCK

**Summary**: The scoped-join architecture, passphrase chain, and tests are strong, but three security/correctness findings must land before merge: (1) the new `DAP_*` env secrets are never registered with the redaction pipeline, so plaintext channel keys/hub credentials can ride `env` tool results into session JSONL (ticket AC8/AC14 requires the redactor registration explicitly); (2) the pure-Dart `HubMessagingRepository` — the only hub path the Flutter app can use — cannot open `fanet1` frames that this PR's own CLI fabric now sends, so app-side DAP channel mail from CLI agents is silently dropped; (3) a private membership whose key fails to decrypt is misclassified as PUBLIC and the fabric then sends unencrypted payloads into a private channel.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 DAP env secrets (`DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` plaintext privs, `DAP_CLIENT_SECRET`, `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE`) absent from `buildSecretRedactor` — no masking, no AC8 byte-scan test (comment1).

tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read the contents of a text file or image. Text output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large text files. Images are returned as base64 content.

## Path selectors

Append a trailing selector to `path` to read exactly the lines you need:

- `:N` — start at line N (1-indexed), through end of file. `:N-` is the same.
- `:A-B` — inclusive line range (`:A..B` works too).
- `:A+C` — C lines starting at A.
- `:R1,R2,…` — multiple ranges, sorted and merged (`:5-16,960-973`); blocks are joined with a `…` separator and ranges past end of file are reported as skipped.
- `:raw` — verbatim content: no line numbers, no hashline header, no notices. Combine as `:raw:50-100` or `:50-100:raw`.

Do not combine `offset`/`limit` with a path selector. Selectors only apply to text files (not images).

## Archives

Read inside `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`/`.tgz` files: `archive.zip` lists the root, `archive.zip:dir/` lists a directory, `archive.zip:inner/file.txt` reads a member (selectors apply, e.g. `archive.zip:inner/file.txt:50-60`). Binary members return a note.

## SQLite databases

When the host supports it, `.db`/`.db3`/`.sqlite`/`.sqlite3` paths read as databases: `data.db` lists tables, `data.db:table` shows the schema plus sample rows, `data.db:table:key` fetches one row by primary key (or rowid), `data.db:table?limit=20&offset=40&order=col:desc&where=...` pages a table, and `data.db?q=SELECT ...` runs a raw read-only query.

## Hashline mode

Set hashline=true to prefix lines with line numbers and a [path#TAG] content-hash header for anchoring hashline edit patches (line numbers stay correct on ranged reads). Suppressed by `:raw`.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file, creating parent directories as needed. Overwrites the file if it already exists.

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
1:def greet(name):
2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)
4:greet("world")
```

Insert a guard after line 1:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.POST 1:
+    if not name: name = "stranger"
```

Replace line 2 with two lines:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
SWAP 2.=2:
+    greeting = "Hi"
+    msg = f"{greeting}, {name}"
```

Delete line 3:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
DEL 3
```

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:
+# generated header
INS.TAIL:
+greet("everyone")
```

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
```
[PLAN.md#A1B2]
INS.POST 2:
+- task
+  - nested task
```
</example>

<anti-patterns>
# WRONG — `-` rows / bare context lines do not exist. The range deletes; the body is only the new content.
SWAP 3.=3:
    msg = "Hello, " + name
-   print(msg)
+   return msg
# RIGHT
SWAP 3.=3:
+   return msg

# WRONG — a pure insertion done as a widened `SWAP`: you want to add one line after 2,
# but you replace 2.=4, retype the keepers, and risk dropping one.
SWAP 2.=4:
+    msg = "Hello, " + name
+    extra = compute(name)
+    print(msg)
# RIGHT — touch nothing you keep; the new line is the whole body.
INS.POST 2:
+    extra = compute(name)
</anti-patterns>

<critical>
If you remember nothing else:
1. RE-GROUND AFTER EVERY EDIT. Every apply mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — take the next edit's numbers from the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`. Stale tag or surprise? STOP, re-`read`.
2. RANGES ARE TIGHT. Cover only lines that change; a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
3. THE BODY IS THE FINAL CONTENT. Every body row starts with `+`; Markdown bullets use `+- item`, not `- item`.
</critical>

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the working directory; returns stdout and stderr, truncated to the last 2000 lines or 50KB. Timeouts you set are retried automatically (3 attempts total) as [bash attempt N]; environment-default timeouts fail once with the partial output. For long-running commands (builds, servers, watchers) pass background: true — you get the job id immediately and a notice when it finishes; check progress with bash_job. A foreground command still running when the user sends a message is moved to a background job untouched (never killed). A command still running after 60s is moved to a background job automatically (never restarted); carried timeouts are NOT auto-retried — retry if the completion notice reports a timeout.

tools.name: bash_job
tools.description: Manage background shell jobs (from bash background: true). Actions: "status" lists running + last 20 exited (all: true = every job; id = one), "output" tails a log (id, lines), "stop" kills a running job (id).

tools.name: lsp
tools.description:
Query a language server for diagnostics, navigation, and renames. For Dart/Flutter workspaces the Dart analysis server (`dart language-server`) starts automatically on first use; other servers can be added via `.fah/lsp.json`.

## Ops

- `diagnostics {path}` — analyzer errors/warnings for a file. Returns `OK` when clean.
- `definition {path, line, character}` — where the symbol at the position is defined.
- `references {path, line, character}` — every reference to the symbol at the position.
- `rename {path, line, character, newName}` — rename the symbol at the position workspace-wide. The server's workspace edit is applied atomically, so barrel files and imports update together; per-file edit counts are reported.

`line` and `character` are 1-indexed and default to 1.

## Rules

- Prefer this over `bash dart analyze` for a single file; diagnostics come back scoped and severity-sorted.
- Prefer `rename` over manual search-and-replace for identifiers: the analysis server finds every reference, including exports and imports.
- Positions point at the symbol's first letter. When unsure of the exact column, `read` the line first.
- Definition/references results render as `file:line:col` with the source line; follow up with `read` for more context.
- If no server is configured for a file type, add one to `.fah/lsp.json` (servers map with `command`, `args`, `fileTypes`, `rootMarkers`).

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web and return ranked results with [n] citation markers, titles, URLs, and snippets. Runs a provider chain (DuckDuckGo first, keyed providers when configured) and falls through on failure. Follow up with web_fetch on a result URL to read the full page.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch a web page and return its main content as Markdown: headings, link anchors, lists, and code blocks are preserved, navigation and boilerplate are stripped. Known sites (pub.dev) are rendered via dedicated handlers. Use it to read pages found with web_search.

tools.name: config
tools.description: Inspect and edit the fa configuration — the user file ~/.fah/config.yaml and the project .fah/config.yaml — without a shell (the same core the `fa config` CLI verbs wrap, available on every host). ops: check = validate both files with the real parsers (errors/warnings/notes + a final ok/failed line); path = list the config file locations and whether each exists; get = the effective value of a dotted key (project scope wins where it participates); set = a surgical single-key write that validates the edited file BEFORE writing, so an invalid value persists nothing. Config keys are documented in the fa-self-config skill — never invent one; unknown keys are rejected. A set result names the file, scope, old -> new value, and whether the change applies live or at next boot.

tools.name: memory_add
tools.description:
# `memory_add` policy

## What to store

Store only **durable** facts — things that must survive across sessions:

- project conventions, architecture decisions and their rationale;
- user preferences, habits, environment facts;
- key discoveries that were expensive to learn (non-obvious behaviour,
  gotchas, working configurations).

Do **not** store task progress, transient state, or anything derivable
from the repository itself (file contents, git history, current diffs).

## The supersede rule

Facts age. When a problem is **solved** or a fact **changes**:

1. delete the outdated record (`memory_delete` by id or exact text —
   deletions are tombstoned, so the old text cannot be re-captured);
2. add the new fact as a fresh record.

Never leave temporary difficulties, workarounds, or "currently broken"
notes in memory forever. A memory full of solved problems actively
misleads future sessions. If you used a record to fix something, that
record's job is done — supersede it.

Before adding anything, `memory_search` for an existing record on the
topic: update (delete + add) instead of duplicating.

## Scope discipline

- **project scope** (default) lives in the project's memory directory and
  is **public**: it is committed to git and shared with everyone who
  clones the repository. Never store secrets, credentials, personal data,
  or anything you would not put in a public commit message.
- **user scope** is global and private to the user's machine. Use it for
  cross-project preferences and facts about the user.

## Style

- One fact per record, concise and self-contained (readable without the
  conversation that produced it).
- Add concrete tags (see [tag_taxonomy.md](tag_taxonomy.md)).
- Prefer facts with staying power: "tests run with `--exclude-tags
  integration`" outlives "I am currently fixing the test suite".

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Search long-term memory for relevant facts, preferences, or past decisions. Use proactively before tasks that might benefit from prior context.

tools.name: memory_list
tools.description: List recent long-term memory entries. Useful to review what the agent already knows.

tools.name: memory_delete
tools.description: Delete a stale, wrong, or obsolete entry from long-term memory by id. Prefer deleting over rewriting when the fact no longer holds at all.

tools.name: schedule_message
tools.description: Send a delayed message to an agent mailbox (your own by default) — schedule a follow-up task to check on something later. The message wakes the recipient when it fires; it survives restarts.

tools.name: ask
tools.description:
Ask the user one or more structured questions when you need clarification or a decision during task execution.

<conditions>
- Multiple approaches exist with significantly different tradeoffs the user should weigh
</conditions>

<instruction>
- Use `questions` for multiple related questions instead of asking one at a time
- Use `recommended` (0-based option index or exact option label) to mark the default; the UI badges it as "Recommended"
- Set `multiSelect: true` on a question to allow multiple selections
- Use short option labels; put explanatory tradeoffs in an option's `description` instead of merging them into the label
- Omit `options` when the answer is free-form text
</instruction>

<caution>
- Provide 2-5 concise, distinct options per question
</caution>

<critical>
- **Default to action.** Resolve ambiguity yourself using repo conventions, existing patterns, and reasonable defaults. Exhaust existing sources (code, configs, docs, history) before asking. Only ask when options have materially different tradeoffs the user must decide.
- **If multiple choices are acceptable**, pick the most conservative/standard option and proceed; state the choice.
- **Do NOT include an "Other" option** — the UI always offers free-text input alongside your options.
</critical>

tools.name: request_secret
tools.description:
Ask the user for a credential (API key, token, password) that you need and that is not available yet.

<conditions>
- A command or call fails because a credential is missing, or the task clearly requires one
- The secret is NOT already in the "Available secret env vars" list
</conditions>

<instruction>
- Set `name` to the conventional env var name for the service (GITHUB_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, NPM_TOKEN...); the user can adjust it before saving
- Explain in `reason` what you need the credential for — the user sees this text
- After the user saves it, reference it as $NAME in shell commands; the value itself never enters the conversation
</instruction>

<critical>

tools.description: Ask a structured decision model (OpenRouter Decisions API, e.g. inception/mercury-decide:free) typed questions about a state and receive calibrated answers as structured JSON: yes-no questions come back with a probability, choice questions with the picked option plus per-option probabilities, score questions with a calibrated score over the ordered legend.
