tools.name: task_status
tools.description: Check the status of spawned subagents. Without an id, lists ALL subagents with their current state, token usage, and last activity. With an id, shows that subagent in detail.

tools.name: task_observe
tools.description: Read the recent message history of a subagent. Useful to inspect what a child discovered or decided before following up.

tools.name: task_send
tools.description: Send a follow-up message to a subagent. A running child receives it in its inbox at the next turn boundary; an idle (waiting for input) or completed child is resumed in its SAME session with the message. The resume wait is capped (1s): a child that does not respond in time reports the message queued and keeps waking in the background (check task_status). Failed children are continued with task_resume instead. Remote a2a:<name> children cannot be steered or resumed — they have no local session or inbox; follow up with a new task item.

tools.name: task_resume
tools.description: Resume a FAILED subagent, continuing the SAME session: the run appends to the existing JSONL transcript, keeps the same mailbox id and display name, and never mints a cloned "name-2" session. Use this after transient failures (provider quota, network). Steering running/idle/completed children is task_send; respawning a fresh agent is task (the new child links supersedes).

tools.name: task_cancel
tools.description: Abort a running background subagent job by id (see task_status for ids). The child agent is cancelled; already-settled jobs report their state instead.

tools.name: reply
tools.description:
Deliver your explicit answer to the parent agent. Call this when your task output is ready — the text becomes the parent-visible reply. If you never call it, the parent still sees your final message as a completion notice, but an explicit reply is the reliable channel.

REPORT SIZE: per-message budget 8000 chars — split longer reports into ordered agent_message parts (report_id, 0-based part_index, more=false on the last), then a short final manifest reply (report_id + report_parts); the harness validates it. See REPORT SIZE CONTRACT in your system prompt. Never probe the output limit.

tools.name: agent_message
tools.description:
Send a message to another agent: a SIBLING subagent id, "main" for the parent orchestrator (for a final answer prefer reply), an absolute mailbox "<sessionId>/main" to reach another Fa instance sharing this session repo, or "name@machine" to reach a session on another machine (delivered through the A2A gateway; the remote machine must be configured under a2a.servers). A session display NAME from agent_directory works too: "goal_builder" or "goal_builder/main" resolve to that session's live mailbox. The recipient sees the message in its inbox on its next turn; completed siblings are resumed. Unknown ids and full queues are rejected.

REPORT SIZE: budget 8000 chars — split long report bodies into ordered parts (report_id + 0-based part_index). See REPORT SIZE CONTRACT in your system prompt.

tools.name: agent_directory
tools.description: List the agent mailboxes in the messaging fabric that are worth talking to: LIVE mailboxes (registration-backed presence or recent activity), any mailbox holding pending mail, your subagents, and your own address (marked). Each entry shows its session display NAME when known, a short mailbox id, the pending message count, presence ("live" / "busy (run in progress, accepts mail)" / "offline"), the last-activity time for offline entries, and the working directory (home shortened to ~). Declared capabilities render as sub-lines. Stale mailboxes are hidden — pass all: true to list those too (that also shows FULL mailbox ids; the default view truncates them to save tokens). Address a mailbox by its session name via agent_message ("goal_builder", "goal_builder/main", or "name@machine" — a peer on another machine is reachable through the A2A gateway when an a2a.servers entry exists for it); asleep targets are woken with a headless run automatically.

tools.name: task
tools.description:
Your session context is limited. Before performing a user request, think whether the work can be delegated to subagents — orchestrate subagents and deliver the result to the user. If it is a simple ask, just perform it yourself.

Run subagents in parallel by passing multiple items in a single `tasks[]` batch. Execution blocks until every item finishes unless `background` is true — then you receive job ids immediately and results deliver as jobs settle.

# Task Design
- **Agent typing:** Pick each item's `agent` type. Read-only research MUST use `agent: "explore"`. Use the default worker only when no specialist fits.
- **No overhead:** Each `task` MUST instruct its subagent to skip formatters, linters, and project-wide test suites. Run those once at the end.
- **One pass:** Prefer subagents that investigate AND edit in one pass; spin a read-only `explore` only when the affected files are genuinely unknown.

# Inputs
- `context`: Shared project state, constraints, and contracts. Applies to the entire batch; do not duplicate this background into individual tasks.
- `tasks[]`: Array of subagents to spawn.
  - `name`: A stable identifier (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`), used to address the agent (`agent://` urls, job ids). Uniquified per session; generated from the agent type if omitted.
  - `agent`: The agent type running this item. Omitting it gives you the general-purpose worker (`task`) — NEVER pass that name explicitly. Only omit it after checking the agent list below and finding no specialist that fits.
  - `task`: Complete, self-contained instructions. One-liners or missing acceptance criteria are PROHIBITED.
  - `outputSchema`: Invocation-specific JSON Schema. The subagent's final message must then be a JSON document satisfying it; invalid output gets ONE fix retry, then the item fails.
- `background`: Run items as background jobs (default: host configuration). Blocking calls return every item's output in the result.

# Communication
Subagents start blank — no conversation history. Put everything they need into `context` (shared) and `task` (per item). After spawn, the family stays connected:
- `task_send {id, message}`: steer a running child, answer a waiting (idle) one, or RESUME a completed one with follow-up work.
- `task_resume {id, message?}`: continue a FAILED child in its SAME session — same id, same transcript, same mailbox, never a cloned `name-2` session. Use it after transient failures (provider quota, network); `task_send` is for running/idle/completed children, a fresh `task` for a clean restart (the new child links `supersedes`).
- `task_status` / `task_observe`: inspect the family at any time — status, tokens, and the child's recent transcript.
- Children can `reply` (their explicit answer to you) and `agent_message` (sibling↔sibling hand-offs) — a child that finishes without replying surfaces a `completed_without_reply` notice with its final text preview.
- Completed subagents stay addressable: send them more work instead of re-spawning duplicates.
- Remote `a2a:<name>` children cannot be steered, resumed, or observed — they have no local session. Follow up with a new task item against the same `a2a:<name>` agent.

# Waiting is idle, not blocked
- Long-running children (test suites, builds, research): spawn them with `background: true` and END YOUR TURN right after spawning. Completions and inbox mail wake you automatically, and each result arrives as a message — waiting is an idle state, never a blocked turn.
- NEVER park your turn waiting on children (foreground watch loops, blocking re-polls, sleep-style watchers). A parked turn is unreachable: owner messages queue behind it for as long as the wedge lasts.
- If a blocking call is still running when a user message arrives, the call soft-yields to background — do not re-block afterwards; finish the reply and end the turn.

# Format Contracts
`context` format:
# Goal         ← what the batch accomplishes
# Constraints  ← rules and session decisions
# Contract     ← shared interfaces

`task` format:
# Target       ← exact files and symbols; explicit non-goals
# Change       ← step-by-step add/remove/rename; APIs and patterns
# Acceptance   ← observable result; no project-wide commands

# Results
Each item's full output is addressable as `agent://<id>`. For items with an `outputSchema`, the stored output IS the validated JSON object, so typed fields are addressable as `agent://<id>/<dot.path>` (e.g. `agent://Explore/findings.0.path`).

# Report Size
A child report above the per-message budget is never silently truncated: the full redacted text is stored as an `agent://` artifact and the result carries a bounded excerpt, the pointer, and explicit completeness (`complete`/`partial`). Resolve the pointer for the whole report. Chunked reports get a final manifest `reply` the harness validates against the observed parts; missing, duplicated, or out-of-order sets are marked INCOMPLETE.

# Available Agents
### task
General-purpose subagent with full capabilities for delegated multi-step tasks
### explore (READ-ONLY)
Read-only codebase research: rapid analysis, pattern searches, and compressed findings for handoff (uses the smol model role when configured)
### review (READ-ONLY)
Read-only code review specialist for quality and security analysis (uses the slow model role when configured)
### plan (READ-ONLY)
Read-only planning specialist that produces implementation plans without editing code

tools.name: checkpoint
tools.description:
Creates a context checkpoint before exploratory work so you can later rewind and keep only a concise report.

Use this when you need to investigate with many intermediate tool calls (read/grep/glob/etc.) and want to minimize context cost afterward.

Rules:
- You MUST call `rewind` before finishing after starting a checkpoint.
- You NEVER call `checkpoint` while another checkpoint is active in the
  same turn. A checkpoint never spans user turns: if one is left unrewound
  when the turn ends, the next `checkpoint` call auto-closes it (the tool
  result names the closed checkpoint) and proceeds.

Typical flow:
1. `checkpoint(goal: …)`
2. Perform exploratory work
3. `rewind(report: …)` with concise findings

After rewind, intermediate checkpoint messages are removed from active context and replaced by the report. The dropped history stays in the session tree; nothing is lost.

tools.name: rewind
tools.description:
End an active checkpoint. Rewind context to it, replacing intermediate exploration with your report.

Call immediately after `checkpoint`-started investigative work.

Requirements:
- `report` MUST be concise, factual, and actionable.
- Include key findings, decisions, and any unresolved risks.
- AVOID raw scratch logs unless essential.
- You MUST call this before finishing if a checkpoint is active.

Behavior:
- If no checkpoint is active, this tool errors. If the checkpoint already rewound, continue from the retained report instead of retrying.
- On success, the session rewinds, keeps your report as retained context, and closes the checkpoint.
- A successful rewind is final for that checkpoint; repeat calls error.

tools.name: compact_expand
tools.description:
Surface and reopen hidden context segments.

Call with NO arguments to list what is hidden: the index of hidden segments with id, kind, size, and a first-line preview each. Pass `query` to filter and rank that index by keyword — it searches the full hidden content, not just previews, so use it when you know WHAT you need but not the id. Discovery is free: it never consumes the expand budget.

To read a segment back, pass its numeric id or range from a marker as `target` (e.g. `5` or `2-6`). Context markers like `[3:hidden·tool_result·4.2k·"first line…"]` or `[2-6:ckpt·38k→40tok·covers:3,5]` are doors, not gravestones: the underlying records stay on disk.

- Giant segments are paged: pass `page` (1-based) to continue past the first page; each page footer states the exact continue call.
- Expanded content counts toward a per-turn budget; every success states the budget left, and when the budget is exhausted the result says so and resets on the next user turn. Only hidden, checkpoint-covered, or summary-folded records expand — the tool tells you when a record is already visible.
- The session file never changes; an expanded segment may be re-hidden later by compaction.

Prefer a targeted expand over re-reading files when the fact was already in context once, and prefer discovery + query over blind ids.

## Managing segments yourself (tier 2)

Pass `action` with a `target` to manage segments directly, without waiting for pressure:

- `action: "hide"` folds a segment you know is dead weight into its expandable marker immediately — one-line marker stays where the content was, `compact_expand` reopens it any time. Real user turns are never hideable; pair groups hide whole; the most recent turns and pinned segments are rejected with the reason.
- `action: "pin"` shields a segment from every hide/compact path (yours, the judge's, pressure-time LRU re-hide); `action: "unpin"` releases it. Pins render on the marker (`·pinned`) and survive session reload.

Hiding and pinning are session state, not edits: the records stay in the file byte-for-byte.

tools.name: session_search
tools.description: Search the WHOLE session archive (every past turn — hidden, compacted and checkpointed regions included), not just the current context. Use it whenever the user references a past decision, rule, task or artifact ("remember when…", "the rules we made") BEFORE answering from assumption. Returns pointers (id, kind, timestamp, preview), never full content — pull the record back with compact_expand. With mode: "map" it reports the archive structure instead: record-kind counts, hidden/checkpoint totals, checkpoint tree with nesting depth.

# pr-1888: feat(1825): scoped DAP channels, app interop and network management

## Description

## Summary

- Add the `/network` join/list/leave/status flow with session, project, and global channel scopes; live joins, resume/reboot rejoins, union dedup, composer-paste joining, and headless env-only provisioning.
- Store private channel keys only as passphrase-encrypted `dapkey1` entries, with per-channel Keychain passphrases, CI `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE`, and pure-env support. Use per-project identities and session-name hub display names.
- Deliver channel traffic through the normal steering/inbox path and support `agent_message to: "#channel"`, including reconnect, scoped membership, public-channel, and mention handling.
- Add Flutter app DAP enrollment (including web/extension), channel chat with roster and @-mentions, channel/network management, roster access badges, and agent/member removal.
- Interop with fa_network public payloads and self-describing private `fanet1` frames via published `fa_hub_client` 0.2.11.
- Add a manual **Reconnect now** action and clear sticky network-offline state on every fresh socket; a real offline greeting reasserts it. Also guard `AgentNetworkController.start` after disposal.

Closes #1825

## Validation

- `dart analyze` — clean; `dart test test/hub/` — **287/287 passed** after syncing with `origin/main`.
- `flutter test test/network/` — **385/385 passed** after syncing with `origin/main`.
- Full Flutter app suite — **3973/3973 passed** at the dispose-guard commit; the subsequent network-only change was revalidated with the full network suite above.
- `fa_hub_client`: `dart analyze` clean, **120/120 tests passed**, publish dry-run clean; 0.2.11 published and tagged `v0.2.11`.
- Live verification: private channel messages decrypted in both directions between a headless DAP agent and the Flutter app; public showcase traffic received by a keyless agent.
- Core `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: only the five macOS `bash_self_defense_test.dart` failures remain; the identical five were reproduced on a clean `origin/main` worktree, so they are pre-existing and unrelated to this PR.

Dependency source: `IstiN/fa_hub_client` branch `feat/public-channel-payloads` (released as 0.2.11).

```
fa dap import 'wss://hub…/ws?channel=<id>' && DAP_HUB_URL=wss://hub…/ws DAP_CLIENT_SECRET='…' DAP_AGENT_NAME=<name> fa
```

Paste it into the composer or `/network` — the invite, the client secret
and the agent name are parsed together (the command is never executed).
The secret is stored `dapkey1.`-encrypted for session/project scopes and
decrypted only into the live connection; at global scope it stays in
memory (the legacy files have no per-hub credential field). Boot and
resume reconnect with the stored credential automatically. After every
join the wizard prints an explicit LIVE / NOT-live verdict — a stored
membership is never presented as a working connection.

## 15. Scoped channel membership + `/network` (issue #1825)

Joining a DAP hub channel from the TUI takes three steps: `/network` →
paste the invite → pick a scope. No shell, no restart, no file editing.

### 15.1 The `/network` menu

- **Join channel** (default): one paste field accepts every invite form —
  `wss://hub/ws?channel=<id>`, the same with `#pub=P&priv=K`, a bare
  `<channel-id>` (uses the configured hub), or the whole copied
  `fa dap import '…'` command. Then one scope question:
  **session** (default) / **project** / **global**. The join takes effect
  IMMEDIATELY on the live connection.
- **Channels**: joined channels with scope badges, `copy invite`
  (app-compatible string; keyless form for public channels) and `leave`
  per scope — leaving one scope keeps the others; leaving the last stops
  delivery at once.
fa-local/
# Runtime agent working directory (bash job logs, transient state).
# .fah holds local-only junk (logs, sessions, bash_jobs, scratch) — but a

# Reply: DAP env secrets redaction (AC8/AC14)

Fixed on the current head. The env contract is now registered with both masking systems at startup:

- `lib/src/hub/dap_secret_redaction.dart` — `registerDapEnvSecrets(env, {redactor, redactionPipeline})` registers `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` (including each embedded plaintext `priv`), `DAP_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `DAP_KEY_PASSPHRASE` with the legacy exact-value `SecretRedactor` **and** the layered `RedactionPipeline.registerSecret` (the `registerBoth` parity pattern from `buildSecretRedactor`, `lib/src/cli/startup.dart:1063-1071`). `registerDapSecret(value, …)` covers the runtime-resolved secrets (decrypted privs, auto-provisioned passphrases, memory-only hub credentials). Non-secret names like `DAP_HUB_URL` are explicitly not registered, and values below the shared min-length guard are skipped by both systems to avoid false positives.
- Wiring: the plugin host takes a `RedactionPipeline` (`bin/fah_hub_plugin.dart:64`) and passes it into the scoped membership setup (`:387`, `:434`, `:439`), so the registration happens where the env contract is consumed.
- Test (the AC8 byte-scan): `test/hub/dap_secret_redaction_test.dart` — an `env`-dump byte scan asserts none of the three values survive redaction, the pipeline receives the same values, runtime-resolved secrets register too, and empty/short values are skipped. All 4 tests pass on head `855be0e4d9`.

# Reply: pure-Dart hub repository cannot open `fanet1`

Fixed on the current head. `HubMessagingRepository._onChannelMsg` (`lib/src/messaging/hub_messaging_repository.dart:576-608`) now opens inbound channel payloads **fanet1-first**: `hubTryOpenFanet1(payloadB64)` detects the `0x01 || spk(32) || nonce(12) || ct || tag(16)` self-describing layout, extracts the sender pubkey, and decrypts with the channel keypair alone (no whois/senderKey lookup — matching what `client.sendChannelFanet1` puts on the wire). A failed fanet1 open falls back to the legacy dap1 layout (`hubDecryptPayloadWithKeyPair` with the whois sender key), so old producers keep working; the `nonce[0] == 1` collision case is handled by the AEAD fallback rather than a drop.

Tests (TDD): `test/hub/hub_messaging_frames_test.dart` — a fanet1 frame built byte-exactly per the `EnvelopeCodec` layout decrypts with the channel key alone; a legacy dap1 frame still decrypts via whois (interop back); a fanet1-*shaped* legacy payload falls back instead of being dropped. The wire format parity with the app's `EnvelopeCodec` (`flutter_app/lib/network/envelope_codec.dart:30-36`) is byte-for-byte the same layout, and the end-to-end interop was live-verified in both directions (PR description). All tests pass on head `855be0e4d9`.

# Reply: undecryptable private memberships classified as PUBLIC

Fixed on the current head. The public/private send decision no longer depends on runtime decryption success:

- `HubPluginHost._isPublicChannel` (`bin/fah_hub_plugin.dart:228-251`) now decides from the **stored** membership shape — a truly public channel has `pub == null` at rest — exactly as suggested.
- New guard `HubPluginHost.privateChannelKeyMissing` (`:206-226`): stored-private membership (keypair at rest) whose key could **not** be resolved at runtime (missing passphrase / no Keychain hit).
- `HubFabricRepository.send` (`bin/hub_fabric_repository.dart:143-160`): when that guard fires, the send **refuses loudly** (`StateError: refusing to send to #<channel>: the private channel key is unavailable …`) so the composition queues/retries instead of emitting a hub-readable payload. The E2E→plaintext downgrade path is gone.

Test: `test/hub/hub_fabric_repository.dart:150` — a private channel with an unresolved key refuses loudly instead of downgrading. Passes on head `855be0e4d9`.

# Reply: unbounded PBKDF2 iteration count

Fixed on the current head. `lib/src/hub/dap_key_envelope.dart:33-41` adds `dapKeyMaxIterations = 5000000`; envelopes claiming more iterations are rejected **before any KDF work** through the existing `FormatException` path (one clear warning, primary job proceeds), so a committed `.fah/dap.json` or a hostile `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON` entry can no longer stall boot.

Tests: `test/hub/dap_key_envelope_test.dart:117` (`iter above the max is rejected BEFORE any KDF work`) and `:133` (`iter below 1 is rejected too`). Pass on head `855be0e4d9`.

# Reply: wrong-typed `pub`/`priv` crashes the parse

Fixed on the current head. `parseDapEnvChannels` (`lib/src/hub/dap_env_channels.dart:104-120`) now reads `pub`/`priv` tolerantly: a non-string value (an int, a YAML-ism list, etc.) produces a loud `DAP_CHANNELS_JSON[i]: "pub"/"priv" is not a string — skipped (#channel)` warning and the entry is skipped — the documented warn-and-skip contract holds and no `TypeError` can escape into `union()`/`seedOverlay()`/`runtimeEffective()`.

Tests: `test/hub/dap_env_channels_test.dart:68` (`an int priv is skipped with a warning, valid entries still join`) and `:81` (`a list-typed pub is skipped (YAML-ism pasted into the CI secret)`). Pass on head `855be0e4d9`.

# Reply: runtime overlay persists plaintext keys and is never cleaned

Fixed on the current head:

- **Stable name + cleanup**: the overlay is a single stable per-`$HOME` file (`~/.dap/runtime/channels.json`, 0600, rewritten atomically) rather than one file per pid — `bin/fah_dap_scoped.dart` (`seedOverlay` :475, stable-name resolution, `_pruneStaleOverlay` :522 with a keep-on-doubt guard at :546), and `cleanupOverlay` (:493-500) deletes it on shutdown (best-effort; a stale file is replaced by the next boot's `seedOverlay`, so cleanup failing is never fatal).
- **Documented**: the overlay is now an explicit row in the secrets documentation — `docs/dap.md:732` — instead of an unaccounted third location.

Test: `test/hub/dap_scoped_memberships_test.dart:446` (`cleanupOverlay deletes the overlay file (best-effort)`). Passes on head `855be0e4d9`.

# Reply: global-scope join writes plaintext `priv`

Confirmed as a deliberate deviation and now explicit in both places the thread asked for:

- **Join warning** (`bin/fah_dap_scoped.dart`, `_globalJoin`): when a private invite is joined at global scope, the wizard prints a loud warning — *"dap: global scope persists the #<channel> key as PLAINTEXT in ~/.dap/channels.json — byte-equivalent with `fa dap import` (the legacy store has no envelope field). Pick session/project scope for passphrase-encrypted keys."* — alongside the memory-only hub-credential notice.
- **Docs**: `docs/dap.md:737-739` states that global scope persists the invite keypair PLAINTEXT, byte-equivalent with `fa dap import`, because the legacy `~/.dap/channels.json` format has no envelope field, and points to session/project for passphrase-encrypted storage.

The reason is indeed REG-* byte-equivalence with `fa dap import` (the legacy global file has no envelope field), and session/project scopes route through `encryptChannelPriv` as the ticket's table intends. The CLI no longer advertises a silent "private channel joined" — the on-disk posture is disclosed at join time.

# Reply: `_loadProject` drops all memberships on one malformed entry

Fixed on the current head. `_loadProject` (`bin/fah_dap_scoped.dart:291-318`) now iterates per entry exactly like `_loadSession`: one malformed record (including an older record missing the required `scope` field) adds a loud `dap: skipped a malformed project membership` warning to `loadWarnings` and is skipped — the remaining entries still load, so a half-corrupt `.fah/dap.json` can no longer silently unjoin every channel.

Test: `test/hub/dap_scoped_memberships_test.dart:406` (`one malformed project entry warns and keeps the rest`). Passes on head `855be0e4d9`.
